Article Title: ‘You could smell alcohol on his breath’: Rahul Gandhi targets Bhagwant Mann over drug menace
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday slammed Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann , accusing him of failing to tackle the state's drug problem and alleging that he used to smell of alcohol during their time together in Parliament.Addressing the party's 'Insaaf Rally' in Sangrur, Rahul also accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government of being controlled by leaders in Delhi and questioned its ability to curb drug abuse.Recalling his time in the Lok Sabha with the Punjab CM, Rahul said, “I was in the Lok Sabha with him. He (Punjab CM) used to sit with us and tell jokes, right there, sitting among us. By 11:00 am, you could smell alcohol on his breath.”He clarified that drinking was a personal choice but said the chief minister's conduct was relevant to the state's fight against substance abuse.“Now, I am not saying that Bhagwant Mann shouldn’t drink; that is his personal affair. If he chooses to drink, that is entirely his own business. But if you truly want to fight the menace of substance abuse, your Chief Minister cannot be under the influence every single evening. You need someone who will fight for Punjab, someone who genuinely feels the pain caused by drugs, someone who carries the pain of Punjab in his heart,” he said.Rahul further alleged that the Punjab government was being run from Delhi with AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and Union home minister Amit Shah exercising influence over the state government.“People here need a govt that works for Punjab. When the Congress party comes to power, the govt of Punjab cannot be run from Delhi. Our party will run the Punjab government from within Punjab” he said.“Right now, however, the reins are held half by Amit Shah and half by Kejriwal, while Bhagwant Mann just sits there. Punjab is being governed from Delhi,” he added.Rahul also questioned Amit Shah's claim that the drug menace in Punjab would be eradicated within three years.“What timeline did they (Union HM Amit Shah) set for the drug issue?... Within three years? In three years, Amit Shah won’t even be the Home Minister anymore... My assessment is that this govt won’t even last a year. Anyway, Amit Shah claims he will eradicate the drug problem in three years,” he said.Recalling his earlier warnings about the spread of drugs in Punjab, Rahul said opposition parties including the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal had dismissed his concerns at the time.“Many years ago, when I first visited Punjab, I pointed out that the drug menace was spreading there. The opposition, the BJP, the Akali Dal, and others, claimed that Rahul Gandhi knew nothing about Punjab and that drugs were not spreading in the state,” he said.He argued that Punjab needed industries, factories and a strong agricultural sector to create opportunities for people, warning that a lack of economic opportunities could contribute to drug abuse and gangsterism.The Congress leader accused the AAP government of failing to deliver on its promise to eliminate drugs from the state.“The Aam Aadmi Party came to power, and you placed your trust in them, in Bhagwant Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party. They promised that they would eradicate the drug menace. I ask you: where have they eliminated it? From which corner of Punjab have they managed to remove drugs? They are simply incapable of eradicating this menace,” Rahul said.The Congress leader also referred to his challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a face-to-face debate, which he said he had issued a day earlier.“Yesterday, I challenged Narendra Modi to a face-to-face debate. He can make anyone he wants the judge for this debate. I guarantee the nation that Narendra Modi cannot sit before me," Rahul said."I can guarantee that within five minutes of the debate starting I will prove that Narendra Modi is a 'desh-drohi' and Donald Trump controls him,” he added.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann of failing to tackle the state's drug problem. He also accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government of being controlled by leaders in Delhi. The Congress leader also referred to his challenge to PM Narendra Modi for a face-to-face debate.

Article Title: 'He walked into room with tattoos': Rahul Gandhi remembers Sidhu Moosewala at 'Insaaf' rally in Punjab, recalls their first meeting
Article Text:
Recalling the concern he felt during that meeting, Rahul said he had sensed that Moosewala was stepping into a dangerous environment by entering politics. He said he wanted to offer the young singer political protection and help him feel comfortable in the party.

Rahul Gandhi attacks Bhagwant Mann over drug menace

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi fondly remembered late Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala at the party's 'Insaaf Rally' on Wednesday. The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha recalled his first meeting with the singer and described him as an impressive, dynamic and talented young man. Inviting Moosewala's father onto the stage, Rahul Gandhi recounted how the singer had walked into his office with tattoos and made an impression on him even before he had heard any of his songs. He also recalled feeling that Moosewala was entering a dangerous field when he decided to join politics.Rahul said he had not known much about Moosewala when they first met a few years ago. He had not heard his music or even his voice. However, the singer's personality and the impression he made during their interaction led Rahul to induct him into the Congress."A few years ago, I met his son at my office. At that time, I did not know Sidhu Moosewala. I was meeting him for the first time and did not know much about him. He was an impressive young man. He walked into the room with tattoos. I had not heard his songs or even his voice at that time. I was only told that he was a good person, a musician, and wanted to join the Congress party . As politicians, we observe people carefully when they come to meet us.We do not rely too much on their words; we go by our feelings and what our heart tells us about them. He was a dynamic and talented young man, so I inducted him into the party."Recalling the concern he felt during that meeting, the leader of opposition said he had sensed that Moosewala was stepping into a dangerous environment by entering politics. He said he wanted to offer the young singer political protection and help him feel comfortable in the party."During our meeting, a thought suddenly crossed my mind, though nobody had told me anything about it. I felt that he was entering a dangerous field. I don't know why I got that feeling. He was a singer, a dynamic young man, and someone who did not understand politics very well. I felt I should protect him in my own way. I did not mean physical protection; that thought had not even crossed my mind. I meant political protection. He was a young man entering politics, and I wanted him to feel comfortable in that environment."Moosewala was shot dead in May 2022 in Punjab's Mansa district. His killing had triggered widespread outrage and questions over the state's law-and-order situation.Rahul Gandhi had also invoked Moosewala's memory during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. When asked how many seats the INDIA bloc would win, he responded with a seemingly cryptic "295". The number was widely seen as a reference to Moosewala's popular song 295, adding another instance of the Congress leader's association with the late singer.Rahul Gandhi also targeted Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government over the drug problem in the state. Questioning the party's promise to eradicate drug abuse, he asked what parts of Punjab had been freed from the menace since the AAP came to power."The Aam Aadmi Party came to power, and you placed your trust in it. Punjab trusted Bhagwant Mann and the Aam Aadmi Party. What was their promise? That they would eradicate drug abuse. I want to ask you... Where have they eradicated drugs? From which part of Punjab have they managed to eliminate the drug menace? They cannot eradicate drugs."He also alleged that Mann's breath would smell of alcohol during their interactions in Parliament. Rahul said the chief minister would sit with MPs and crack jokes early in the morning, but that the smell of alcohol would be noticeable by 11am.Clarifying that he was not questioning Mann's personal choice to consume alcohol, Rahul said a chief minister leading a campaign against drug abuse could not himself be under the influence of intoxicants."Let me tell you another story about your chief minister. When I was in the Lok Sabha, he would sit with us early in the morning and crack jokes. However, by 11 am, his breath would smell of alcohol. I am not saying that Bhagwant Mann should not consume alcohol. That is his personal matter. If he wants to drink, it is his personal choice. But if you want to fight drug abuse, your chief minister cannot be under the influence of intoxicants every evening. "
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi fondly remembered late Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala at the party's 'Insaaf Rally' The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha recalled his first meeting with the singer and described him as an impressive, dynamic and talented young man. He said he wanted to offer the young singer political protection and help him feel comfortable in the party.

Article Title: 'Debate in Parliament': Himanta Sarma hits back at Rahul Gandhi's challenge to PM Modi
Article Text:
Himanta Sarma responds to Rahul Gandhi’s challenge to Modi

Sarma cites Bofors, Bhopal gas tragedy

Rahul Gandhi challenges PM Modi to public debate

NEW DELHI: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Wednesday responded to Congress leader and leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi's challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a public debate, saying the discussion should take place in Parliament rather than on the streets.In a post on X, Sarma took a swipe at the Rae Bareli MP over his Diwali greeting to the Prime Minister, in which the Congress leader had wished Modi on the festival while holding a rose.“Dear Rahul ji, roses are given on Valentine’s Day, not on Diwali. Anyway, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will see you in Parliament,” Sarma wrote.In a video shared on X, the Assam chief minister questioned whether Rahul was aware of his responsibilities as the leader of the opposition and said Parliament was the appropriate venue for a debate with the Prime Minister.“Rahul ji, yesterday you posted a video. You were holding a rose and wishing the Prime Minister a Happy Diwali. Rahul ji, roses are given on Valentine’s Day; they are not given on Diwali. Tell me one thing: are you even aware that you are the Leader of the Opposition? If you are the Leader of the Opposition and if you truly consider yourself to be one, then where is this debate with the Prime Minister supposed to take place? On the streets? In some alleyway? Or in Parliament?” Sarma said.He also referred to the presence of the Lok Sabha Speaker and members of Rahul's family in Parliament, arguing that the debate could be held there.Sarma said several issues, including the Bofors controversy and the Bhopal Gas Tragedy, could be taken up during a parliamentary debate. He urged former Congress president to initiate the discussion and ensure that proceedings were not disrupted.“There are plenty of issues to discuss, from Bofors to the Bhopal Gas Tragedy. This time, please ensure there is no ruckus in Parliament. You should initiate the debate; the Prime Minister will respond, and all these issues can be addressed,” he said.Questioning the Congress leader's call for a public face-off outside Parliament, Sarma added, “Why do you want to drag people out onto the streets? This isn't Bangladesh; this isn't Nepal. Rahul ji, do not take the people for fools.”He further advised the Congress leader to move away from what he described as the role of an “angry young man” and participate in a peaceful debate in Parliament.The Congress MP had issued the challenge in a post on X on Tuesday, urging PM Modi to agree to a public debate in the presence of the media and the country's youth.“It’s been 24 hours since I challenged you, Modi ji. You say the opposition is anti-national. Choose any stage, any venue, and debate me on this - Who is anti-national? Who has connections with foreign forces? And what is the nature of those connections? Let’s do this as soon as possible. Daro mat!” Rahul wrote.Proposing a format for the discussion, the Congress leader said both leaders could sit across a table, with the Prime Minister free to appoint the moderator.“We’ll both be there. The media will be there. The youth of this country will be there. There will be a table. You’ll sit on one side, I’ll sit on the other. You can appoint whoever you want as the judge. You can even make Mohan Bhagwat ji the judge,” he said.Rahul also listed several issues he wanted to raise, including the financial system, the India-US deal, the Adani case and the Epstein matter.“There will be questions about the financial system, the financial structure, how the US deal happened, why it happened and why so quickly, why you made the deal alone and didn’t inform the Cabinet, why the Adani case was closed, Epstein - and many other issues. We’ll discuss all of them openly.Let the truth come out. Let everything be crystal clear,” he added.The Congress leader also challenged PM Modi to file a defamation case against him over his allegations, saying he was already facing several such cases.“You make allegations against me, don’t you? Come forward. Everything will become clear. You’ve filed defamation cases against me over other matters. I think there are around 45 defamation cases against me. But on this issue of the debate, on the question of foreign connections, you haven’t filed a defamation case. Go ahead, file one. We’ll discuss that openly too. Happy Diwali, Modi ji,” Rahul wrote.
Article Summary: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma responds to Rahul Gandhi's challenge to PM Modi for a public debate. Sarma questions whether Rahul is aware of his responsibilities as the leader of the opposition. He says Parliament is the appropriate venue for a debate with the Prime Minister.

Article Title: PM Modi calls Sharad Pawar; advises complete rest
Article Text:
The 85-year-old veteran politician was admitted to a private hospital in Pune on Monday, then discharges 2 days later

We along with Supriya will look after the country, you focus on recovery, PM tells Pawar

PUNE: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday called NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar to enquire about his health after the veteran politician was discharged from a private hospital in Pune."Prime Minister Modi called up Pawar Saheb this morning to enquire about his health. He spoke with great warmth and respect and suggested that Pawar Saheb take complete rest," Vitthal Maniyar, a close associate of Sharad Pawar, told the media in Pune on Wednesday.Maniyar said PM Modi urged Pawar not to worry about work and to focus on his recovery."The PM told Pawar Saheb that Supriya is now ready and that he, along with Supriya, will look after the country, while Pawar should focus on his health," Maniyar said.Pawar thanked the Prime Minister for enquiring about his health and assured him that he would take rest.The 85-year-old veteran politician was admitted to a private hospital in Pune on Monday morning after complaining of pleuritic pain. After undergoing treatment for two days, he was discharged on Wednesday.In an official statement, Dr Purvez K Grant, chairman and managing trustee of Ruby Hall Clinic, said, "Sharad Pawar has been discharged from the hospital today. He is stable and doing well. He will be travelling directly from the hospital to his residence in Mumbai."
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi called NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar to enquire about his health. The 85-year-old veteran politician was admitted to a private hospital in Pune on Monday, then discharges 2 days later. PM Modi urged Pawar not to worry about work and to focus on recovery.

Article Title: FIR against Prashant Bhushan for sharing fake video of Russian minister criticising India
Article Text:
FIR against Prashant Bhushan for sharing fake video of Russian minister criticising India

An FIR has been registered against senior advocate Prashant Bhushan for sharing a morphed video purportedly showing Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov criticising India over its internal affairs and oil purchases.The development comes a day after the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) fact-checked the video, confirming that the clip was fabricated. The clarification followed a denial by the Russian Embassy, which also disputed the authenticity of the video.Bhushan had shared the clip on social media with the caption, "a tight slap by the Russian foreign minister on India. What kind of advice was Jaishankar giving to Russia?"The video purportedly showed Lavrov criticising India's domestic affairs and its purchases of Russian oil.This comes as External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met Lavrov on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta, US, on October 31.Jaishankar shared a photograph of the meeting on X, saying, “Discussed the Ukraine conflict, Gulf situation and multilateral issues with FM Sergey Lavrov of Russia.”Addressing queries during the MEA's bi-weekly press briefing, spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Jaishankar had held several bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the G20 gathering, including one with his Russian counterpart.The meeting between the two ministers covered the Ukraine conflict, the situation in the Gulf and wider multilateral issues.The interaction took place amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war and heightened tensions in West Asia, which have raised concerns over energy security, maritime trade routes and regional stability.India has continued to engage with Russia through high-level diplomatic meetings despite differences between Moscow and Western capitals over the Ukraine conflict. New Delhi has consistently maintained that dialogue and diplomacy are essential to resolving international disputes.At the G20 gathering, Jaishankar also emphasised the importance of diplomatic engagement over military action, maintaining that military solutions alone cannot resolve complex global challenges.
Article Summary: FIR against senior advocate Prashant Bhushan for sharing fake video of Russian minister criticising India. The video purportedly showed Lavrov criticise India's domestic affairs and its purchases of Russian oil. This comes as External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met Lavrov on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta.

Article Title: One more Indian seafarer killed near Oman; toll 23
Article Text:
Indian seafarer Gandhar Nahim Ajij from Gujarat killed after a vessel was struck by an unidentified aerial object near Oman, taking the number of Indians killed in the West Asia conflict to 23

NEW DELHI: An Indian seafarer died in an attack on a commercial vessel near Oman, taking the toll of Indian nationals killed in the West Asia conflict to 23. Of these 23 Indians, 15 were seafarers.India condemned the attack on MSV AL JUSUFI near Limah in Oman. On Tuesday, shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal on X said on Nov 2 (Monday), the Indian vessel carrying 14 Indian seafarers was struck by an unidentified aerial object while navigating near the Oman coast. "While 13 crew members safely evacuated and were rescued by Omani Coast Guard, I am deeply saddened to report that one of our seafarers, Gandhar Nahim Ajij from Gujarat, tragically succumbed to injuries," he said.In a statement, MEA said the continuing attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply concerning and reiterated India’s call for immediate deescalation of tensions, and the conclusion of ongoing negotiations for a diplomatic solution so that peace and stability can return to the region. “The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways in the region, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest,” it said.Responding to a question on Russia-Ukraine conflict, also said that five Indians had been killed so far in attacks in the Black Sea region. Officials said that so far, 4,330 Indian sailors have been brought back safely from the conflict-hit Persian Gulf. They added that currently there are eight Indian-flagged ships in the Persian Gulf and six of them are operating in that region.“Two foreign-flagged ships carrying fertilisers are waiting to transit through the Strait of Hormuz,” said an official.
Article Summary: An Indian seafarer died in an attack on a commercial vessel near Oman, taking the toll of Indian nationals killed in the West Asia conflict to 23. Of these 23 Indians, 15 were seafarers. Officials said that so far, 4,330 Indian sailors have been brought back safely from the conflict-hit Persian Gulf.

Article Title: Judge facing rape charge presides over Pocso court
Article Text:
SC seeks Allahabad HC's response to a rape complainant's plea to suspend a UP judge who has been chargesheeted for rape and heads a POCSO court.

NEW DELHI: Can a UP additional district judge, chargesheeted for rape by Delhi police for allegedly sexually exploiting a woman, head a Pocso court which decides criminal cases against persons accused of sexually assaulting minors? Supreme Court has agreed to examine this petition filed by the rape complainant.A bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice Monday on the petition and sought response from Allahabad high court on her plea for suspension of the senior judicial officer.Appearing for the petitioner, advocate Rakesh Kumar Singh told the bench that at least judicial work should be withdrawn from the judge, but the Allahabad HC had rejected her petition.The bench in a cryptic order said, "Issue notice, returnable on Dec 11."The petitioner had lodged an FIR at Mayur Vihar police station on Dec 8, 2022 accusing the judicial officer, whom she met on a matrimonial site, of making repeated false promises to marry to establish a physical relationship with her.Delhi Police in Jan 2023 sought permission from Allahabad HC to proceed against the judicial officer. Two months later, Delhi HC granted the judge interim protection from arrest but allowed police to continue the investigations, she said.Police later recorded her statement before a magistrate.Police in June 2023 sent a reminder to Allahabad HC for early decision on request to proceed in investigations against the judicial officer but were informed by the HC that a vigilance inquiry was already going on against him. In Oct 2024, the chief justice of Allahabad HC permitted investigations, and the HC directed the judicial officer to cooperate with the probe.In April 2025, Delhi police informed the Allahabad HC regarding proposal to file chargesheet against the judge and on May 5 last year, the chargesheet was filed against the additional district judge under Section 376 IPC (rape). In Nov last year, Delhi HC allowed the trial court to proceed with the chargesheet but continued the interim order protecting the judicial officer from arrest.On May 23, the chief metropolitan magistrate of Karkardooma courts in Delhi took cognisance of the chargesheet, leading the complainant to file a petition before Allahabad HC seeking suspension of the officer. She moved SC after HC declined her plea.
Article Summary: SC seeks Allahabad HC's response to a rape complainant's plea to suspend a UP judge who has been chargesheeted for rape and heads a POCSO court. The bench in a cryptic order said, "Issue notice, returnable on Dec 11."

Article Title: Indian tourist killed, PIO injured as copters collide during Everest rescue
Article Text:
Indian killed as copters collide during Everest rescue

Here's what happened

(With agency inputs)

A 47-year-old tourist from Chennai was killed and two others - an Indian-origin New Zealand citizen and a pilot - were injured when two helicopters collided barely about 10 feet above a helipad near Mt Everest on Tuesday. The accident occurred around 8.11am at Pheriche, 12km south of Everest Base Camp, as one helicopter was evacuating tourists stranded by heavy snowfall and the other was carrying cargo.The rotor blades of the two choppers struck each other as both aircraft attempted to land, sending them crashing onto the snow-covered helipad. Aviation authorities suspect miscommunication between the pilots, who were operating beyond the coverage of the nearest air traffic control tower in Lukla - gateway to the Everest region. The accident is believed to be Nepal's first mid-air collision involving two helicopters.The deceased was identified as Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu, who died at the scene. Shailesh Krishna Patel (49), a New Zealand citizen, and Fishtail Air pilot Rabindra Prajapati sustained injuries. Balaramudu and Patel were being evacuated aboard a private Fishtail Air Airbus AS350 helicopter, registration 9N-AJR, which had taken off from Gorakshep, a remote settlement near Everest Base Camp at an altitude of approximately 5,164 metres.The other helicopter, an Air Dynasty AS350 registered 9N-AOD, had flown from Lukla carrying cargo. Its pilot, the sole occupant, escaped unhurt. Verified footage showed the helicopters approaching the helipad from different directions, with one descending faster than the other.The weather appeared clear, with no visible signs of strong winds. People nearby rushed towards the wreckage immediately after the collision. “Preliminary reports suggest miscommunication between the pilots, as the area is outside the coverage of Lukla Airport’s air traffic control tower and pilots have to communicate with each other,” said Mukesh Dangol, director general of the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal.“We are recording the statement of the injured pilot,” he added. CAAN spokesperson Gyanendra Bhul said, “It appears the accident happened when two helicopters attempted to land at the same spot.” The aviation authority has launched an investigation to establish how both aircraft came to approach the helipad simultaneously. Solukhumbu district official Kaman Singh Thapa Magar also confirmed that the weather was clear at the time but raised the possibility of a technical problem.Prajapati and Patel were flown by a Prabhu Air helicopter to Nepal Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu Valley.Air Dynasty confirmed that its pilot was uninjured, contradicting initial reports that both pilots had sustained injuries. Balaramudu’s body was first taken to Lukla and later transported to Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu for a post-mortem before repatriation to India.India’s foreign ministry said the Indian embassy in Kathmandu was coordinating with Nepalese authorities to bring back Balaramudu’s remains. Pheriche, at around 4,300 metres, is a key stop along the Everest trekking route. Heavy snowfall had disrupted trails and left tourists stranded at high-altitude settlements, including Gorakshep, prompting helicopter evacuations. Expeditions are under way on Everest and nearby Ama Dablam.With no road access to the upper Everest region, choppers are widely used to ferry climbers and supplies, besides carrying out rescues.
Article Summary: Vasanth Kumar Balaramudu, 47, died at the scene. Shailesh Krishna Patel (49), a New Zealand citizen and Fishtail Air pilot Rabindra Prajapati sustained injuries. Aviation authorities suspect miscommunication between the pilots, who were operating beyond the coverage of the nearest air traffic control tower.

Article Title: Major fire breaks out at HPCL Visakhapatnam refinery, no casualties
Article Text:
A fire occurred at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited Visakh Refinery during the night, alarming nearby residents.





VISAKHAPATNAM: A fire that broke out at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited's (HPCL) Visakhapatnam refinery in Malkapuram on Monday night was brought under control, with no casualties or injuries reported.The fire was confined to a pitch intermediate storage tank in the refinery's sulfur unit, and all units at the facility are operating safely, HPCL said.In a post on X, the company said the fire was reported around 10pm on November 2, following which its Fire and Safety Team immediately activated firefighting and emergency response measures."The fire was localised to the pitch tank area and was brought under control within a short time. There have been no casualties," HPCL said, adding that all refinery units were functioning safely.Malkapuram Circle Inspector E Narasimha Rao said the fire involved sulfur pitch, a waste or bottom product generated in the refinery's sulfur unit. He said HPCL's own fire tenders were deployed to tackle the blaze and no external assistance was required."There are no casualties, no injuries and no major issues. Everyone is safe, and there is no need for panic," he said.Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) Dileep Chakravarthy, who visited the site, said the fire had been completely extinguished using the firefighting equipment installed at the refinery and resources deployed by the Andhra Pradesh Fire Department.He said a small blast was reported at the facility before the fire broke out. Chakravarthy added that an enquiry would be initiated to examine industrial safety at the facility in accordance with applicable norms."There is no cause for worry, and no injuries or casualties have been reported. People are requested not to panic about the incident," he said.Meanwhile, eyewitnesses said the flames rising from the refinery were large enough to frighten people in the vicinity. One eyewitness said people moved away from the area after seeing the blaze.
Article Summary: A fire broke out at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited's (HPCL) Visakhapatnam refinery on Monday night. No casualties or injuries were reported. The fire was confined to a pitch intermediate storage tank in the refinery's sulfur unit.

Article Title: Dilip Ghosh takes 'Sonia' jibe at Mamata for joining INDIA bloc rally against SIR
Article Text:

Festive season security arrangements

Ghosh targets Mamata over development boards

NEW DELHI: West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh on Tuesday criticised former chief minister Mamata Banerjee for attending the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Taking a dig at Mamata, he said that she was turning to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi for leadership out of "utter helplessness".Ghosh claimed that Banerjee's party has lost political ground in its state and that she was seeking political relevance by aligning with the Congress leadership.“Earlier, she set out to become the top leader herself. Now, she has nothing left in her hands. Today, she isn’t even an elected representative. That is why, out of utter helplessness, she goes around accepting Sonia ji as her leader again. Her party is finished today,” news agency ANI reported, quoting Ghosh.He also hit out at Banerjee over her objections to the electoral process, saying political parties must respect the people's mandate. He alleged that she had no complaints about the Election Commission or democracy when her party was winning elections.“As long as she was winning, democracy was fine, and the Election Commission was fine. The moment she lost, everything went wrong. Keep faith in the people; the people decide who wins and who loses. One must accept the verdict of the public,” he said.The minister further claimed that the removal of fake voters during the electoral roll revision had paved the way for free and fair elections in West Bengal. He alleged that Banerjee had benefited from such voters in previous elections.“Look, when the revision occurred, the fake voter base through which Mamata used to win was eliminated. Once they were separated, a free and fair election took place. A genuine election happened in Bengal after many years, and people are happy about it; change has arrived. No outsider can simply enter and become a citizen of this country or avail benefits here,” he said.Ghosh also said the ruling government and party workers would organise rallies across the state to counter the Opposition's attempts to create unrest and communicate their position to the public.“It is also our responsibility to make people understand and deliver the right message. The people are nationalist, and the government is nationalist. No one will be permitted to create unrest in the country. We will also reach out to the people and hold rallies everywhere; this is just the beginning,” he said.Meanwhile, Ghosh said the state government was making arrangements to ensure that Deepavali, Kali Puja and Jagaddhatri Puja celebrations passed off peacefully.He said every cabinet minister had been assigned a district to oversee law and order during the festive season. Ghosh has been given responsibility for Purba Medinipur, also known as East Midnapore.“The government is keeping a close watch across all of West Bengal to ensure that the upcoming Deepavali, Kali Puja, and Jagaddhatri Puja are conducted smoothly and with enthusiasm. Every cabinet minister has been assigned the responsibility of overseeing law and order in one district. I have been given charge of Purba Medinipur (East Midnapore). I am also meeting with them to ensure all arrangements are in place and nothing goes wrong. This is the government’s duty, and the public must cooperate,” he said.The minister also criticised the previous Trinamool Congress government over the functioning of development boards set up for marginalised communities, including the Matua community.He alleged that several boards formed during Banerjee's tenure had not received adequate funds or been given meaningful work.“Mamata Banerjee had formed several development boards in West Bengal: the Rajbanshi Board, the Matua Board, the Bhumij Adivasi Board, but gave neither funds nor work to anyone. She only played politics,” he said.Ghosh said the Matua community, many of whose members migrated from Bangladesh, continued to face economic hardships and needed focused development measures. He said the board should be made functional and provided with funds.“Now, for that community, especially the Matua community, most of whom came from Bangladesh, have numerous hardships and are poor. Their development must happen; therefore, the board must be actively functional for them, and funds must be provided, which our chief minister (Suvendu Adhikari) has initiated," he said.
Article Summary: West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh criticised former chief minister Mamata Banerjee for attending the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Article Title: Right to protest can't justify endless occupation of a site: SC
Article Text:
SC says no group or political outfit can occupy a protest site indefinitely, stresses need to balance the right to protest with traders’ and daily-wagers’ livelihoods

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday said no group, political party, NGO or civil society outfit could occupy a protest site indefinitely.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said there were competing fundamental rights right to carry on trade and business and right to free speech and expression when senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, appearing for traders, said the court must restrain all parties, NGO and civil society groups from holding protests in Delhi for the next two months to enable businesses to resume and to ensure that workers got their due.The court asked a traders’ association, which has sought Rs 1,000 crore in damages due to protests by CJP and opposition INDIA bloc during the festive season, to implead the protest organisers in the case for determination of compensation and how it is apportioned if it is awarded.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said those who call for bandhs and agitations must bear responsibility towards compensating the loss caused to others. The bench asked Rohatgi to make the individuals, organisations and political parties responsible for protests and the resultant closure of shops parties in the petition.When senior advocates Menaka Guruswamy, Arundhati Katju, N Hariharan and others simultaneously argued that protests were part of the right to free speech and right of dissent in a democracy, the bench said, “The right to protest and right to trade and business are both constitutionally recognised fundamental rights.We are not talking about trade in the commercial sense.”CJI Kant said, “We are talking in terms of the source of livelihood of daily wagers, hawkers, rediwalas, sabziwalas – where will they go? Hence, a protest site must be identified which allows people to protest without hampering the livelihood of daily wagers.” The CJI emphasised that the right to protest was not an absolute right. “One set of protesters cannot occupy a designated protest site for all times to come... Everyone has a right to protest and they should be given a definite time period to protest...,” he added.Mehta said, “Calling for a protest without permission and asking people to march to Parliament cannot be permitted.” On denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar said the decision was taken based on the recommendations of a committee constituted following the SC’s July 2018 order for regulating protests at Jantar Mantar.“The proximity of the new Parliament premises has further enhanced the significance of regulating activities in the surrounding areas, having regard to the security and uninterrupted functioning of a vital constitutional institution."
Article Summary: The court asked a traders’ association, which has sought Rs 1,000 crore in damages due to protests by CJP and opposition INDIA bloc during the festive season, to implead the protest organisers in the case. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said those who call for bandhs and agitations must bear responsibility towards compensating the loss caused to others.

Article Title: EC: Okay to use Form 6 for re-inclusion in rolls
Article Text:
Section 31 of the RP Act provides for imprisonment up to a year or fine or both, for anyone making a false declaration during updation of rolls

EC clarifies deleted voters can seek re-inclusion through Form 6 during SIR without facing prosecution for false declaration

Declaration prescribed under Form 6 has been in force since Aug 1, 2022: EC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Election Commission Tuesday clarified that no action will be taken against a previous elector, whose name is deleted from draft rolls published during Special Intensive Revision (SIR), who seeks re-inclusion by filling Form 6.The declaration that the voter's name is being included in the electoral roll for the first time will not be liable for prosecution under election laws for making a false statement, EC said in a communication to chief electoral officers (CEOs) of states and UTs.Recalling a Delhi HC order dated Oct 14 that held as "misplaced" the apprehension of an applicant, who argued that submitting Form 6 would amount to making a false declaration, EC directed that "no action shall be initiated under Section 31 of the R P Act by an ERO against an elector merely on the ground that the elector had been included in a previous electoral roll and has submitted Form 6 during the SIR process or afterwards, provided the elector is not already enrolled in any other parliamentary or assembly constituency and the declaration made is otherwise in accordance with law".Stating that submission of Form 6 for inclusion afresh under SIR or afterwards is not, by itself, false merely because the elector was previously enrolled, EC on Tuesday instructed chief electoral officers of states and UTs that no action should be initiated by electoral registration officers (ERO) against such electors under Section 31 of the Representation of the People (RP) Act, 1950. Section 31 of the RP Act provides for imprisonment up to a year or fine or both, for anyone making a false declaration during preparation or updation of electoral roll.Certain previous electors, whose names did not figure in the draft electoral roll published during SIR, have been hesitant to submit Form 6 as they are also required to furnish a declaration prescribed in Form 6 that their name is being included for the first time in the electoral roll.They believe that this would amount to falsehood in view of their previous enrolment, attracting Section 31. Stressing that the declaration prescribed under Form 6 has been in force since Aug 1, 2022, the poll body clarified that an elector whose name does not appear in the draft electoral roll may submit Form 6 to seek inclusion in the final electoral roll, “in accordance with the prescribed procedure,” both under SIR and afterwards, irrespective of whether such elector was enrolled previously.
Article Summary: EC clarifies deleted voters can seek re-inclusion through Form 6 during SIR without facing prosecution for false declaration.Declaration prescribed under Form 6 has been in force since Aug 1, 2022: EC. Section 31 of the RP Act provides for imprisonment up to a year or fine or both, for anyone making a false declaration during updation of rolls.

Article Title: 'Radical thinking': INDIA bloc allies snub Left leader Neha Bora's 'Brahmanvaad' remark

Neha Bora at a press conference at the CPI(ML) Liberation Parliamentary Office in New Delhi.

NEW DELHI: Congress's key ally, Samajwadi Party , has unequivocally distanced itself from the "Brahmanvaad" remark of Left-wing student leader Neha Bora.The AISA president, under the patronage of INDIA bloc leaders, gained limelight for fiercely criticising the poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar and the electoral roll purge under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).On Bora's "need freedom from Brahmanvaad" remark, Samajwadi Party's Rajeev Rai said: "Making such a sweeping statement is not appropriate. Every religion has both good and bad people; we shouldn't make such generalisations... We should avoid them. That is exactly what the BJP wants; why should we fall into their trap?"Rai, who represents the Ghosi Lok Sabha constituency in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, firmly repudiated the AISA leader's rhetoric riddled with "sweeping generalisations"."In this day and age, the kind of rhetoric being used is simply unacceptable. There is no basis for it. We shouldn't make sweeping generalisations about any caste, community, religion, or region," he said.Akhilesh Yadav's party is not the only one to shrug off Bora's statement, as Uddhav Sena leader Priyanka Chaturvedi also called her assertions "unfortunate", saying radical thinking, be it from the Right or the Left, is harmful to the nation."It is highly unfortunate. She reportedly referred to the Unnao and Kathua cases while making her remarks.Bhandari also linked her comments to an earlier statement by Rahul Gandhi on the safety of women."Neha Bora poster girl of Rahul Gandhi displays her Hindu hate," Bhandari wrote.He added, "She is inspired from Rahul Gandhi who earlier had said 'Mandiro main ladkiyon ke sath ched chad hoti hai'.""Congress Hates Hindus, loves vote bank! Congress Soch is a threat to India's unity!" Bhandari posted.The remarks triggered a political row after the video surfaced on social media. However, the clip is undated, and the circumstances in which Bora made the comments could not be independently verified.Bora has been actively involved in protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.She took part in an October 10 demonstration organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student groups in Delhi. Police detained several protesters, including Bora, as restrictions on public gatherings were imposed in parts of the capital.The AISA president also backed the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally against the CEC, urging people to join the opposition's demonstration in Delhi.She has also appeared alongside Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders during protests against the poll body chief. Article Title: Judge needn't face strictures for typos in judgement: SC
Article Text:
SC sets aside Rajasthan HC’s strictures against a trial judge over inadvertent errors in a judgment, ruling that the remarks were unwarranted as the errors did not affect the case outcome

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Some factual errors in a judgement delivered by her, allegedly due to a 'cut, copy and paste' job, had cost a trial judge dear, resulting in Rajasthan HC castigating her and sending her to a judicial academy for training. But Supreme Court has come to the judge's rescue and struck off the adverse observations against her, holding that criticising a judicial officer for inadvertent typographical errors in a judgement, which did not affect the outcome of the case, was unwarranted.A bench of Justices Sandeep Mehta and Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya allowed the plea of the judge and expunged the strictures and adverse remarks against her."Ex facie, we feel that the adverse observations and the strictures recorded by HC against the judicial officer were uncalled for and avoidable. These disparaging remarks and the strictures were recorded on the judicial side without affording an opportunity to the judicial officer to show-cause or to place her explanation on record before such observations and strictures were made, and hence, suffer from the vice of nonadherence to the principles of natural justice," it said.HC observed the judicial officer "had used the methodology of 'cut, copy and paste' and in all probability, the judgement had been scripted by the stenographer/clerk concerned and was signed without being read and corrected by the presiding officer as she failed to strike out the irrelevant paragraphs which related to the trial of the adult accused".The trial judge had passed two judgements arising out of the same case as one of the accused was a minor. After appreciating the evidence in both trials, the judicial officer pronounced separate judgements convicting both the accused of the charges against them and sentencing each to 20 years' RI.SC said it seemed that during the course of rendering judgements in the two cases, some extracts of evidence/numerical details from one trial were inadvertently incorporated into the judgement for the other.
Article Summary: SC sets aside Rajasthan HC’s strictures against a trial judge over inadvertent errors in a judgment. Justices Sandeep Mehta and Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya allowed the judge and expunged the strictures and adverse remarks against her.

Article Title: 1.5-tonne Nasa space observatory set to crash on Earth today, possibility of debris parts falling in India
Article Text:
File photo: Nasa's 1.5-tonne Swift space observatory is set to re-enter Earth's atmosphere on Wednesday after 22 years, with some debris possibly falling over southern India.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A 1.5-tonne space observatory of Nasa is heading back to Earth on Wednesday after working in space for 22 years and some parts of its debris could fall in southern India.Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory was launched in 2004 to explore the universe’s most powerful explosions called gamma-ray bursts. When launched, the spacecraft was a first-of-its-kind multiwavelength observatory designed to study the most powerful explosions in the cosmos using its three telescopes.“US Space Force predicted that the spacecraft will re-enter the atmosphere at approximately 3:30 a.m. EST, Nov. 4, with an uncertainty of 11 hours,” Nasa said on Monday.The US space agency expects most of the spacecraft to burn up as it travels through the atmosphere, but some components are expected to survive re-entry.Most surviving debris is expected to fall into the ocean. However, parts of India, Africa, Australia, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America could fall within the possible re-entry zone.The re-entry band spans between 20.6°N and 20.6°S latitude, which covers parts of southern India (including cities like Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Bhubaneswar and Kochi).Isro has not said anything if it is tracking the descending space telescope.“If 70% of the Earth is ocean, 30% is land. So three out of 10 times it's on land, not ocean,” Brad Tucker, an astrophysicist at Australian National University, told ABC News.The Nasa observatory was originally designed for a two-year prime mission.However, the spacecraft was able to conduct science operations for more than two decades. Swift served as a multi-tool for exploring the universe, observing a wide range of light, rapidly pointing at short-lived outbursts, and sending alerts to other facilities to help coordinate follow-up observations.“The observatory has broadened our understanding of a wide variety of cosmic objects and events, from active galaxies powered by supermassive black holes and stars undergoing X-ray flares, to supernova explosions and comets and asteroids in our own solar system,” Nasa said.
Article Summary: Nasa's 1.5-tonne Swift space observatory is set to re-enter Earth's atmosphere on Wednesday after 22 years. The US space agency expects most of the spacecraft to burn up as it travels through the atmosphere, but some components are expected to survive re-entry. Most surviving debris is expected to fall into the ocean.

NEW DELHI: Union minister Hardeep Puri is set to win the upcoming Rajya Sabha bypoll unopposed from Madhya Pradesh after the nomination papers filed by two candidates were rejected by the returning officer.According to news agency PTI, the nominations of Congress-backed candidates Rajkumar Lohani and Kante Sayanna were rejected on the last day of scrutiny.Meanwhile, the two independent candidates, along with Congress leader Hemant Katare, also objected to Puri's nomination papers, contending that his affidavit in Form 26 was invalid and incomplete.However, returning officer Umesh Sharma examined the objections and held that Puri had not violated any requirements of the Representation of the People Act."No defect was found in Puri's papers," the returning officer said in his order.Congress termed the order an "attack on Indian democracy" and said it would move court against it."This is an attack on Indian democracy. The last date for filing nominations is November 2, while scrutiny will take place on November 3. Candidates can withdraw their nominations until November 5.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday expressed gratitude to Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck after a sacred Buddhist stupa was dedicated to him in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Bhutan.In a social media post, PM Modi said he was "deeply touched" by the special gesture of warmth and generosity shown by the King and the people of Bhutan, adding that he accepted the honour with gratitude on behalf of the people of India.He described the Jangchub Chorten as an enduring symbol of the shared spiritual and civilisational heritage and friendship between the two countries.In a separate social media post, the Bhutanese King said the 76th Stupa was dedicated to Prime Minister Modi on November 1, after 108 stupas were raised in Gelephu Mindfulness City.King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck, along with India's Union minister for parliamentary affairs Kiren Rijiju, unveiled a plaque dedicating the stupa to Modi.The King said the dedication was an enduring symbol of his "profound appreciation" for PM Modi's unwavering commitment and India's steadfast support for the realisation of his vision for Gelephu Mindfulness City.The 108 Jangchub Chortens form part of Bhutan's effort to highlight its Buddhist heritage and spiritual identity through the Gelephu Mindfulness City project.The dedication of the 76th stupa to PM Modi adds a diplomatic dimension to the initiative, reflecting the close relationship between the two neighbouring countries. NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday flagged the alleged open sale of conventional and uncertified firecrackers in Delhi markets despite its recent order allowing only certified green crackers ahead of Diwali.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale referred to a media report published on Tuesday, which highlighted the availability of different varieties of firecrackers in several markets across the national capital, according to Bar and Bench.The bench asked Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati to look into the alleged violations."In today's report, there's a photograph, they say that notwithstanding yesterday's order, now everything is available in the (firecracker) shops. Please look into it," Justice Sundresh told Bhati.The judge also referred to the report's claims that licensed and unlicensed crackers, including those with and without QR codes, were being sold openly."They say that in the market every other cracker, licensed, unlicensed, QR code, or no QR code, everything is available. Please take a note of it," he said.Also read: SC on Diwali: Crackers on Nov 7-8 in 2 time slots, and keep it green On November 2, the Supreme Court allowed the sale of certified green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR from November 4 to 6 and their use on November 7 and 8, subject to restrictions.Firecrackers can be burst only between 6am and 7am and 8pm and 10pm on these two days. A complete ban will be restored from November 9.The court had clarified that only firecrackers certified by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) and the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO) could be manufactured and sold.It also restricted sales to designated locations and prohibited online sales. Each box must carry a product-specific QR code to verify its certification. The manufacture of firecracker strings, or laris, and crackers containing barium was also prohibited.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday flagged the alleged open sale of conventional and uncertified firecrackers in Delhi markets. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale referred to a media report published on Tuesday. The judge also referred to the report's claims that licensed and unlicensed crackers, including those with and without QR codes, were being sold openly.

Article Title: 'Can't occupy a site for all times': SC on Delhi protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Article Text:
A traders' counsel told the court that around 50 lakh people lived in areas surrounding the protest site and claimed that shops remained shut

Absolutely, it promotes fairness No, all groups should have indefinite access Depends on the circumstances 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday said no protest group can occupy a designated demonstration site indefinitely, observing that the right to protest must be balanced with the rights of other citizens. Hearing pleas filed by traders' associations over the impact of demonstrations in Delhi, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said designated protest venues must be made available to different groups for specific periods."You can't occupy a site for all times. Where farmers, journalists, etc. will go? Everyone has right to protest. Designated time must be given for designated period," CJI Surya Kant said, according to LiveLaw.The bench also said that orders granting permission for protests must clearly specify the reasons for allowing or refusing them. "You can't prevent other people, that I am doing protest now you can't," the CJI observed.The court was hearing pleas raising concerns over alleged police brutality, mass detentions, the closure of Metro stations and internet shutdowns during protests, besides the impact of demonstrations on businesses.A traders' counsel told the court that around 50 lakh people lived in areas surrounding the protest site and claimed that shops remained shut, with virtually nobody visiting Connaught Place. The court issued notices to the Centre and other authorities on a plea by the Kirana Committee Delhi seeking a halt to protests during the festive season.However, the bench said it could not adjudicate the traders' grievances unless all organisations involved in the protests were made parties to the proceedings. It asked the traders' associations to implead the organisers of the anti-CEC protests.The hearing comes weeks after the Centre de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, identifying Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as alternative venues for demonstrations.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said designated protest venues must be made available to different groups for specific periods. The bench also said that orders granting permission for protests must clearly specify the reasons for allowing or refusing them. The court issued notices to the Centre and other authorities on a plea by the Kirana Committee Delhi seeking a halt to protests.

Article Title: Rank-based merit list to replace percentile for NEET PG: Panel to SC
Article Text:
NMC gives in-principle approval to replace percentile-based NEET-PG and NEET-SS counselling with a rank-based system, under which only candidate ranks would be declared

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Medical postgraduate admissions could see a major change, with the National Medical Commission (NMC) giving in-principle approval to replace the existing percentile-based system with a rank-based system for NEET-PG and NEET-Super Speciality (SS) counselling.A 12-member expert committee constituted to review the NEET-PG admission and counselling process told Supreme Court in its report on Tuesday that the commission is working on a new regulation under which only ranks would be declared and percentile marks would no longer be specified.The proposal received in-principle approval at the NMC's meeting on Sept 23, according to a letter dated Oct 1, 2026, from the NMC secretary to the director general of health services (DGHS). The commission is yet to finalise the regulation.SC is examining various petitions challenging Centre's decision to drastically reduce the qualifying cut-off percentiles for NEET-PG 2025. Under revised criteria, the qualifying score for general category was reduced from 276 to 103, while that for SC/ST/OBC categories was brought down from 235 to minus 40.The report was filed after detailed deliberations and consideration of suggestions made by senior advocate Maninder Singh, who is assisting the Supreme Court as amicus curiae."NMC is in process of issuing new regulations, which are yet to be finalised wherein only rank-based system for NEET PG & SS counselling will be adopted; no percentile marks will be declared in results; only ranks will be given to candidates. A letter dated Oct 1 has been written by secretary, NMC to DGHS informing proposal for changing existing percentile-based system to a rank-based merit system for NEET-PG and NEET-SS which is under consideration by the Commission.The panel has accorded in-principle approval for proposed change with a view to address the issues arising from the existing system," the report said.On reduction of minimum qualification, the report said, "sanctity of NEET examinations should be maintained and minimum qualifying standards in postgraduate medical education is not diluted to the extent of permitting candidates with grossly inadequate or negative performance to become eligible for admission; the significance of competitive examinations should not be reduced to an administrative formality. "It also suggested that there should be no salary discrimination between residents of clinical and non-clinical branches and incentives should be given to doctors to work in rural areas.
Article Summary: National Medical Commission (NMC) gives in-principle approval to replace existing percentile-based system. NMC is in process of issuing new regulations, which are yet to be finalised. No percentile marks will be declared in results; only ranks will be given to candidates.

Article Title: SC to define right to privacy of protesters in public places
Article Text:
SC agrees to examine privacy rights of protesters amid concerns over Delhi Police’s use of CCTV cameras and facial recognition technology

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Tuesday agreed to examine the contours of right to privacy of people when they are part of a public protest as lawyers appearing for recent protesters in the capital claimed breach of privacy because of the deployment of CCTV cameras and facial recognition tools by Delhi Police.Appearing for a petitioner, political activist and advocate Prashant Bhushan told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that deployment of facial recognition tools as well as CCTV cameras, and the use of data generated by them required scrutiny so that they were not put in the public domain or used for harassing young protesters.Solicitor-general Tushar Mehta said CCTV cameras were installed for the safety of protesters. He added that fears of anti-social and criminal elements mingling with protesters to cause damage to public property and resort to violence came true during CJP's "illegal" July 20 march to Parliament call. "It was primarily to ensure the safety of women," he said.Justice Bagchi said CCTV surveillance may not per se violate the right to privacy but if that data was fed into a machine for facial identification and tracing history of an individual, then it may amount to breach of privacy."It has to be examined whether this action infracts privacy," he added.Senior advocate Mahesh Jethmalani interjected and said the court was only determining the constitutional rights of protesters. What about the rights of innocent citizens whose daily lives and livelihoods got derailed by these protests, he asked and suggested that the court devise an SOP for protests to fasten liability on the organisers for loss and damage to public property and loss of livelihood.The SC said the Identification of Prisoners Act, replaced by the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Act, 2022, empowers the state to identify people by using iris data and those provisions need to be kept in mind. The SG said though the case did not involve prisoners, the law does empower govt to collect data for interests of the state.Justice Bagchi said, "When a person stands in a public place, what is his reasonable expectation?" The SG replied, "One cannot choose to protest in a public place and seek protection of privacy."When Justice Bagchi said it was a competing right - right to privacy and legitimate state interest - Mehta said it was strange that protesters had no problem with scores of live TV channels broadcasting them or swarms of influencers making reels and uploading them on social media but had a problem with govt's CCTVs.Mehta said no iris verification of protesters was ever done by police. The bench said police had said they had matched the IDs of people with NCRB database of criminals. "Does that amount to a legitimate state interest?" it asked. Mehta said after facial recognition, the person concerned with a criminal track record was investigated and called for inquiry.The bench issued a notice on Bhushan's petition and tagged it with petitions questioning deployment of facial recognition tools .
Article Summary: Supreme Court agrees to examine the contours of right to privacy of people when they are part of a public protest. Lawyers appearing for recent protesters in the capital claimed breach of privacy because of the deployment of CCTV cameras and facial recognition tools. Solicitor-general Tushar Mehta said CCTV cameras were installed for the safety of protesters.

Article Title: ‘You remember neither promises nor skullcap’: NCP MP Aga Ruhullah quits, takes aim at Omar Abdullah
Article Text:
Aga Ruhullah Mehdi resigns from National Conference after 24 years, accuses Omar Abdullah of betraying party promises
